chapters: A Tale of Three Intersecting Lines

mock.title: CHAPTER 1 · LARGE NUMBERS AROUND US
question: What is the
product
of all the numbers on a telephone dial-pad?

tryit.text: The sum of the ages of Shubham and Shivam is 36. What will the sum of their ages be after 36 years?
tryit.think: Think of you and a friend. In one year, how much older does each of you get?

tryit.text: In ‘8 @ 7 − 15 < 4 × 2 × 5’, which operator cannot be used in place of ‘@’, so that the condition stays true?
tryit.think: Begin with the easy side: work out 4 × 2 × 5 first.

tryit.text: Using the digits 1, 2, 3 and 4, form the highest and the smallest three-digit numbers that each contain exactly two different digits. What is the sum of the two numbers?
tryit.think: Split it into two jobs: build the highest number, then the smallest. Add them at the end.

tryit.text: The sum of the ages of four people A, B, C and D is 35. Each of them is at least 8 years old. What is the MAXIMUM possible age of the oldest person?
tryit.think: Say it simply: “To make one person as old as possible, how old should the other three be?”

tryit.text: An equilateral triangle and a square have sides of the same length. What can you say about the areas of the two shapes?
tryit.think: I know the triangle can fit inside the square. Draw them on the same side to see.

tryit.text: A 2-digit number has two different digits. Reversing its digits makes another 2-digit number. Which can the difference between the two numbers NOT be: even, odd, prime, or a whole number?
tryit.think: Try 21 − 12 and 41 − 14. Ask why every difference is a multiple of 9.

tryit.text: Two decimal numbers differ by 3.6. Moving the decimal point one place to the right in one of them makes the two numbers equal. Which was the smaller number?
tryit.think: Write it in numbers: if the smaller is n, the bigger is 10 × n. Their difference is 3.6.

backcover_intro: In Class 7, children take Computational Thinking further: reading large numbers, building and testing expressions, and reasoning through puzzles one clue at a time. These are not just computer skills. They are thinking skills for every subject.
